material_systems.name: Residential Wall Repaint — Standard
notes: Standard residential repaint; spot prime repairs, two finish coats.

material_systems.name: Residential Wall Repaint — Enhanced
notes: Enhanced residential; light sand between coats, tighter edge discipline.

material_systems.name: Residential Wall Repaint — Premium
notes: Premium residential; full sand/inspect between coats, tape-line edges preferred.

coverage_profiles.notes: Applied to repairs, stains, bare spots only; coverage based on repair area not total wall SF.

usage_rate.notes: 3/8 or 1/2 nap for smooth walls; higher quality uses more covers for fresh nap.
2.5-3 inch angle sash for cut-in; freehand strategy increases brush wear.
Only used with tape_line edge strategy; delicate surface tape for residential.
Canvas drops for furniture/floor protection in occupied residential.
Nail holes, minor dings; fair condition increases usage significantly.
Gap filling at trim/ceiling transitions; more needed in fair condition.
150-180 grit for between-coat sanding; QL-3 minimal, QL-5 full sand.
Dust removal after sanding; higher quality = more frequent tacking.

compatibility_rules.rule: Test existing coating adhesion before proceeding; glossy surfaces require scuff sanding.
compatibility_rules.risk: Adhesion failure if existing coating is incompatible or poorly adhered.
compatibility_rules.mitigation: Include adhesion test in prep; scuff sand glossy surfaces.

compatibility_rules.rule: Stain-blocking primer required for water stains, smoke damage, or tannin bleed.
compatibility_rules.risk: Bleed-through of stains within weeks of finish application.
compatibility_rules.mitigation: Spot prime all stains with shellac or pigmented shellac primer.

compatibility_rules.rule: Use delicate-surface tape in residential to avoid damage to existing finishes.
compatibility_rules.risk: Tape removal damages adjacent trim, ceiling, or existing wall paint.
compatibility_rules.mitigation: Use low-tack/delicate surface tape; remove at proper timing.

risk_notes: Dark-to-light color changes may require tinted primer or additional coats beyond spec.
Textured walls reduce tape effectiveness and may favor freehand cut-in.
Low-VOC requirements in occupied homes may limit primer options.
assumptions: Standard latex interior paint unless specified otherwise.
Consumable rates are placeholders pending field calibration.
Spot prime coverage assumes 5-10% of wall area for good condition, 15-25% for fair.
uncertainty_flags: Actual spackle/caulk usage varies widely by home age and condition.
Brush consumption for freehand cut-in needs field validation.
